tools.name: bcdev_test_discover
tools.description: Scan the AL project for test codeunits ([Test] methods, with each method's attributes and TransactionModel) and TestRunner codeunits (with TestIsolation). Also reads compiled packages: appFile inspects one .app, alpackages: true adds every .app in <project>/.alpackages (dependency or Microsoft test apps, e.g. fetched with bcdev_package_download), so their codeunit IDs can be passed to bcdev_test_run. Filesystem only — no server needed.

project.description: AL project directory (default: server cwd); source for .vscode/launch.json connection defaults and .al file scanning

appFile.description: Path to one compiled .app (absolute, or relative to the project). Inspects only that package; the workspace .al scan is skipped (tests and runners are empty).

alpackages.description: Also inspect every .app directly in <project>/.alpackages (default false). Results go to packages; unreadable packages to warnings.

tools.name: bcdev_test_select
tools.description: Pick the AL test methods a Git diff can affect, before running anything: changed procedures and triggers are expanded through the whole-program call graph (al-sem `alsem graph`, else altool; BC_DEV_CALLGRAPH_ENGINE) to the [Test] methods that may execute them, and unioned with an optional coverage map from an earlier bcdev_test_run. Returns a ranked selection (direct > event > dynamic), uncoverable changed procedures (with al-sem: no test can reach them, under the graph's stated assumptions), shards whose codeunits feed bcdev_test_run unchanged, and fallbackToAll when the diff is outside what selection can see. Limit: the tests must be in the same app as the code (or a test folder nested in it); with a separate test app selection falls back to the whole suite. Local only (git + alsem/altool); no server needed.

baseRef.description: Git base ref (for example origin/main). Its merge-base with HEAD is compared to the working tree, including untracked AL files, exactly as bcdev_test_run coverageAgainst does.

coverageMapFile.description: Coverage map written by an earlier bcdev_test_run coverageMapFile, relative to the project. Adds coverage-history evidence; without it selection is static reachability only.

maxCodeunitsPerShard.description: Maximum test codeunits per shard (default: one shard)

tools.name: bcdev_test_run
tools.description: Run AL tests on the BC server. Per-method results and optional procedure coverage (coberturaFile writes it as Cobertura XML for CI); coverageAgainst also reports which Git-changed procedures this run did not exercise.

coverage.description: Code coverage. 'procedure' reports which procedures each test reached. Line-level coverage is not available: Business Central sends line data only over the Dev API 8.0 coverage-export protocol, which BC28/BC29 servers (Dev API 7.0) do not offer. Default 'none'.

coverageAgainst.description: Git base ref for changed-procedure gap analysis (for example origin/main). Compares its merge-base with HEAD to the current working tree, includes untracked AL files, and requires/implies procedure coverage.

coverageMapFile.description: Write a versioned per-test procedure-coverage map (format bc-dev-mcp.coverage-map v1: test codeunit/method name/methodId -> covered procedure identities, stamped with the coverageAgainst merge base) to this JSON file, relative to the project. Requires/implies procedure coverage; overwrites the file.

coberturaFile.description: Write procedure coverage as Cobertura XML (the layout of altool runtests --coverage-format cobertura) to this file, relative to the project; overwrites it. One class per AL source file with project-relative filename, one method per procedure (hits = number of tests that reached it, 0 when none). Requires/implies procedure coverage. Test codeunits and triggers are omitted.

changesDeployed.description: Explicit assertion that the current working-tree versions of changed AL objects are deployed to this server. Required for covered/uncovered classifications because procedure coverage does not carry an app or source hash.

tools.name: bcdev_test_orchestrate
tools.description: mode 'repeat' (default): run one AL test selection sequentially 2–20 times, retain every enriched attempt, diff adjacent passed/failed sets, and flag flaky or incomplete method outcomes. mode 'order': run each method alone, then the selection recorded, reversed and once per seed; classify od-victims (pass alone, fail after others), bisect each to its polluter, and optionally attribute the polluter's writes to pollutionTableId. When al-sem is installed (BC_DEV_ALSEM), a static pre-screen predicts polluter -> victim pairs (committed writes to a table a later method touches); the bisect probes them first and each pair is reported confirmed/refuted/unresolved. Reports each method's TransactionModel and the project runners' TestIsolation. Needs local AL source. Non-rolled-back test side effects repeat on every attempt.

tools.name: bcdev_debug_attach
tools.description: Attach the AL debugger to the BC server. By default it binds the next client; sessionId selects an existing NST session and userId filters the next client. Attach returns before binding — use bcdev_debug_wait for sessionBound and later events. One debugger session at a time. Returns debugSessionId, an opaque handle to pass to every bcdev_debug_* follow-up (optional there; it must match when given); it stays valid until bcdev_debug_detach or server restart.

tools.name: bcdev_debug_wait
tools.description: Wait for the next debugger event (sessionBound, break, testRunFinished, detached, fatal). Timing out is a normal result — call again to keep waiting. Events queue up to 100 between calls; beyond that the oldest are discarded and droppedEvents reports how many. A detached event before any break usually means a stray session bound at attach time (common with breakOnNext WebServiceClient on BC28): nothing was debugged, so bcdev_debug_detach and attach again after about 10 seconds.

debugSessionId.description: debugSessionId returned by bcdev_debug_attach; valid until bcdev_debug_detach (or server restart). Optional: omitted uses the single active debug session; given, it must match the active one or the call fails NOT_FOUND.

effects.description: On a break event, also report what the top frame's routine can still do (commit, table writes, errors, UI) via al-sem. Optional: absent al-sem yields effects.status=unavailable, never an error.

tools.name: bcdev_debug_continue
tools.description: Resume from a break: continue, stepOver, stepInto, or stepOut — then bcdev_debug_wait for the next event. abort terminates the paused operation (a bound test run reports it as failed); release lets it run to completion undebugged. Both end debugging with a detached event.

debugSessionId.description: debugSessionId returned by bcdev_debug_attach; valid until bcdev_debug_detach (or server restart). Optional: omitted uses the single active debug session; given, it must match the active one or the call fails NOT_FOUND.

action.description: continue resumes; step actions advance one statement (over/into/out of calls); abort kills the paused operation and detaches; release lets it finish undebugged and detaches — re-attach to debug again

frameId.description: Stack frame index from the break event: 0 = innermost frame

expand.description: Dot-joined variable path to expand, e.g. 'Customer' or 'Customer.Fields'. Segment names come from the variable list; global variables live under '<Globals>'.

tools.name: bcdev_record_writes_start
tools.description: Arm background record-write triage for one numeric table ID. Business Central breaks globally; the collector identifies each runtime receiver, groups exact target stacks, and auto-continues. Trigger the matching workload after start, then check status and finish. A next-session or user-filtered attach whose bound session detaches before any break (a stray bind; about half the attaches with breakOnNext WebServiceClient on BC28) is re-armed automatically after ~10 s, up to maxRearms; status shows phase rearming, and a workload started during that window is missed, so trigger it only after status has shown phase arming for about 2.5 s (a stray detaches within milliseconds of an attach). Returns recordingId, an opaque handle to pass to bcdev_record_writes_status/finish (optional there; it must match when given); it stays valid until bcdev_record_writes_finish or server restart.

tools.name: bcdev_native_list
tools.description: Discover the dynamic Business Central 28 native MCP tool catalog for business actions, AL runtime, or the active paused debugger. Use the returned input schemas with bcdev_native_call. On-prem: uses BC's MCP endpoint on the API/OData port (needs McpServicesEnabled). Plain http:// sends Basic credentials unencrypted — use it only for local/dev containers. context='debugging' on-prem is unverified (only business and runtime were seen live).

tools.name: bcdev_snapshot_start
tools.description: Arm a snapshot debugging capture on the BC server: the next matching session records the variables at each snappoint (an AL line, 1-based) and at any error it throws, without pausing it. After this, TRIGGER the scenario (open the page in a browser or business-central-mcp), call bcdev_snapshot_status until ready, then bcdev_snapshot_finish to get decoded points. clientType WebClient is verified (also with userId or a running sessionId). WebServiceClient is experimental and records nothing usable: it binds an API/OData call, but Business Central drops the capture when that short session ends, so status/finish report it lost. Background is experimental and records nothing usable on BC29: it binds a TaskScheduler/job session, but the archive holds only source while it runs and BC drops the capture when it ends. ClientService is experimental and unverified. To capture an AL test run, call bcdev_snapshot_run_tests after start (verified on-prem). One capture (profile or snapshot) at a time per tenant. Captured variables can contain customer data, credentials and source code; they are returned to the agent as-is (no redaction), and the saved zip holds everything, even what the response omitted.

tools.name: bcdev_snapshot_status
tools.description: Status of the active snapshot capture: Initialized (no session bound yet; trigger the scenario), Started (recording; ready to finish), Finished or Failed (finish to collect or release it).

snapshotId.description: snapshotId returned by bcdev_snapshot_start; valid until bcdev_snapshot_finish (or server restart). Optional: omitted uses the single active snapshot capture; given, it must match the active one or the call fails NOT_FOUND.

tools.name: bcdev_snapshot_finish
tools.description: Finish the snapshot capture, save the recording zip and decode it into points (exceptions first, then snappoint hits) with variables, call stack and a source window. decodeStatus: decoded | empty (nothing recorded) | raw (zip saved, converter unavailable) | failed (failedStage + error; zipPath when saved). The capture is released once the server answers. With debuggingContext (and connection params) it recovers a capture this process does not hold; pass the start's snappoints to classify them. Default save folder: <os temp>/bc-dev-mcp-snapshots; bc-dev-mcp never deletes saved zips. Captured variables can contain customer data, credentials and source code; they are returned to the agent as-is (no redaction), and the saved zip holds everything, even what the response omitted.

tools.name: bcdev_snapshot_run_tests
tools.description: Run AL test codeunits attached to the armed bcdev_snapshot_start capture, through Business Central's native snapshot MCP run_tests, so the capture records the test run (a failing test's exception and variables). Needs an armed capture from bcdev_snapshot_start; on-prem only (cloud is refused). Returns per-method results (failed tests are ordinary results); then call bcdev_snapshot_finish to collect the recording. Uses the capture's connection; the MCP endpoint is on the API/OData port (apiPort, default BC_DEV_API_PORT or 7048). Test messages and BC errors can contain application data.

tools.name: bcdev_symbols_download
tools.description: Fill <project>/.alpackages with every symbol package the project's app.json needs: platform System, the Application concept, declared dependencies, and all their dependencies. Downloads only what is missing at a satisfying version (sequential, one request each) and reports each package as downloaded/replaced/unchanged/skipped/failed. dryRun lists the app.json references and their local-cache status without a connection.

tools.name: bcdev_app_uninstall
tools.description: Uninstall the installed version of an app through the Automation API. Business Central also uninstalls every installed dependent app, without warning; those are reported in alsoUninstalled. deleteData: true also deletes the app's data. Uninstalling without deleteData keeps the app's data, and Business Central then refuses to publish a lower version of it; pass deleteData: true when you intend to downgrade or start clean. Returns alreadyUninstalled when the app is published but not installed (nothing is deleted then, even with deleteData).
